title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth homepage introduces a service that creates personalised, illustrated family storybooks from family members and a shared memory. It offers a free digital preview, printed hardcovers, links to pricing and process information, and a prominent 'Log in' button.
output.think_aloud: This looks relevant to me because I would like a story about Sam and Grandpa Joe at the beach. The illustration is appealing, but words like 'multimodal generative narrative engine' and 'lived-experience corpus' sound far more technical than the simple family product I understand.

site_model.what_it_is: A website that turns family details and a remembered event into a personalised illustrated storybook.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting a story featuring their child and another favourite person.
site_model.value_proposition: Create a bespoke family memory story, preview it digitally, and optionally have it printed as a hardcover.
main_tasks: Check and potentially order a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: A free digital preview is advertised; the cost of printed hardcovers is not yet shown, though a Pricing link is available.
trust_signals: A stated StoryHearth Ltd company footer
Customer testimonials with first names and UK cities
site_model.fit_for_me: It sounds well suited to preserving a memory involving Sam and Grandpa Joe, especially because I can preview the story before deciding on printing.

page_review.purpose: Explain the family storybook service and direct visitors to pricing, login, or the story creation process.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page displays a warm family-oriented hero area, an illustrative book image, a three-step explanation, testimonials, and frequently asked questions below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: Attractive and relevant, though the main paragraph sounds unnecessarily technical and makes the service feel less approachable.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try logging in and creating the Sam and Grandpa Joe story.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the dark 'Log in' button at the top right is immediately noticeable.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, 'Log in' clearly matches what I need to do.

issues.title: Unnecessarily technical product language
issues.evidence: Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I have to work out what the service actually does, and the jargon makes it feel less warm and trustworthy for a family keepsake.
issues.fix: Replace this with plain language such as: 'Turn a family member and a treasured memory into a personalised illustrated storybook.'

issues.title: Testimonials provide few trust details
issues.evidence: “My daughter asks for ‘her’ book every single night.” — Hannah, Leeds
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The quote sounds nice, but I cannot tell whether it comes from a real verified customer or gives any useful information about the finished product.
issues.fix: Mark testimonials as verified customer reviews and show fuller reviewer details or link them to independent reviews.

positives: The warm illustration makes the product feel child-friendly.
The three process steps clearly explain the basic workflow.
'Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK' is useful and easy to understand.
The prominent login and proceed controls are easy to find.

output.memory_note: A free digital preview is available, but printed hardcover pricing is not shown on the homepage.
output.plan: I will use the clearly visible 'Log in' button, sign in with the supplied account, and then create the beach story with Sam as the hero and Grandpa Joe as the second character.

title: Log in – StoryHearth

output.observation: The StoryHearth login page presents a simple form under “Welcome back” with empty email and password fields and a “Log in” button. Links for account creation, privacy, terms, and contact are also visible.
output.think_aloud: This is straightforward. The placeholders tell me which details belong in each box, and the orange button makes the main action obvious.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — clicking “Log in” on the previous page clearly navigated me to the login screen, as shown by the “Welcome back” form and changed URL.

page_review.purpose: This page lets an existing StoryHearth customer sign in to their account.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page displays two empty credential fields, a “Log in” button, and a link to create an account. The navigation also offers “How it works” and “Pricing.”
page_review.first_impression: It looks calm, simple, and easy to understand. I can immediately see what I need to do.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to log in so I can create the storybook.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the two large input boxes and the orange “Log in” button are immediately noticeable.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The “Email” and “Password” placeholders and “Log in” button match what I want to do.

issues.title: Email and password fields have no persistent labels
issues.evidence: [5] and [6] are listed as “textbox (no label)” and rely only on the placeholders “Email” and “Password”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The placeholders make the form understandable visually, but persistent labels would make it clearer which field is which and more accessible.
issues.fix: Add visible labels such as “Email address” and “Password” associated with each input, rather than using placeholders as the only labels.

positives: The form is uncluttered and the main action is visually prominent.
The wording is familiar and easy to understand.
There is a clear route to create an account for anyone who is new.

output.memory_note: Login credentials are demo.family@storyhearth.test and Bedtime-2026.
output.plan: I will enter my email and password in the two fields, then click “Log in” to access my account and start creating the family storybook.

output.observation: The dashboard confirms that login succeeded and shows an empty library: “Welcome back, Demo,” “You have no books yet,” and a prominent “+ Create a new book” button. The orange “+ Create a new book” button is obvious, so I’ll use that and see whether I can still enter the story details.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the dashboard heading and “My books” page clearly show that login worked, but the unexplained “profile sync incomplete” warning makes me unsure whether everything is fully working.

page_review.purpose: Show the signed-in user’s saved books and provide a way to create another book.
page_review.what_is_happening: The site has logged in the Demo account and presents an empty book library with a creation button. A prominent error banner reports that profile synchronization is incomplete.
page_review.first_impression: The page is simple and the next action is obvious, but the technical error makes me question whether my account information has loaded correctly.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating a book because that is my next step.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the orange “+ Create a new book” button stands out immediately.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create a new book” clearly matches what I want to do.

issues.title: Unexplained technical sync error
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether my family details are missing, whether creating a book will work, or what I should do about it.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-language message such as “Some profile details may not have loaded. You can still create a book, or try again,” and provide a visible Retry option.

issues.title: Error gives no recovery action
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.” with no visible retry or help control
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am left wondering whether the page is genuinely broken and what to do next.
issues.fix: Include a “Try again” button and a “Continue anyway” option if book creation is still available.

issues.title: Generic account greeting
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It is functional, but using the actual account name would feel more reassuring and personal.
issues.fix: Personalize the dashboard with the user’s name or email identifier where appropriate.

positives: The successful login destination is easy to recognize as the dashboard.
The empty-library message is concise and easy to understand.
The main action is clearly visible and clearly labelled.

output.memory_note: The dashboard displayed an unresolved “profile sync incomplete” warning.
output.plan: I will click “+ Create a new book,” then enter the beach memory with Sam as the hero and Grandpa Joe in the story. I will watch for any further sign that the sync error affected my profile.

output.observation: The page is a form for choosing the child who will star in the story and another person to include. I can enter Sam's details, her appearance, Grandpa Joe's name, and their relationship before continuing.
output.think_aloud: This form is clear enough, and the orange “Next” button stands out. It asks about the people first, but I still need to get to a place where I can enter our memory at the beach.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the click on “+ Create a new book” clearly opened the “Create your book” form.

page_review.purpose: Collect the details of the child and the other person who will appear in a personalised story.
page_review.what_is_happening: I am logged in and viewing empty character fields with a Next button. The form starts with Sam's name, age, pronouns, and optional appearance, followed by Grandpa Joe's name and relationship.
page_review.first_impression: It looks tidy and easy to scan. “Who's the star of the story?” makes the purpose friendly, although “Who else is in the story?” sounds as though I might be able to add more than one person even though there is only one name field.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I can fill in the known details and continue.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the fields, dropdowns, and orange Next button are all visible without needing to search.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. The labels match what I want to enter, but “Who else is in the story?” implies multiple additional characters while the form only provides one name field.

issues.title: Singular character field contradicts plural wording
issues.evidence: The heading says “Who else is in the story?” but there is only [10] “Who else is in the story?” textbox.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I may think I have missed controls for adding several people, or assume Grandpa Joe's name needs to be written in an unusual combined format.
issues.fix: Change the label to “Who is the other person in the story?” if only one person is supported, or add a clear “Add another person” control if multiple people are allowed.

issues.title: Optional appearance field may be too restrictive for the planned memory
issues.evidence: [9] “What do they look like? (optional)” has placeholder “e.g. curly red hair, green welllies” and there is no field for Grandpa Joe's grey hair.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Sam can be described, but the second person may not be visually represented accurately unless there is another step or free-text detail field.
issues.fix: Allow appearance details for the additional character too, or clarify that this description applies to both characters.

positives: The main action is an obvious orange “Next” button.
Required character information is grouped logically on one screen.
The age and pronouns dropdowns reduce the chance of entering inconsistent wording.

output.memory_note: I still need to enter the memory: a day at the beach building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe, with Sam as the hero.
output.plan: I will enter Sam and Grandpa Joe's details, keep Grandpa Joe selected as a grandparent, and click Next. Then I will look for the screen where I can enter the beach memory.

page_review.purpose: To preview the completed personalised storybook and provide access to further pages and hardcover ordering.
page_review.what_is_happening: A 9-page preview is displayed with the cover of “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.” The cover is labelled “A StoryHearth original” and “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.” A disabled previous arrow, page indicator 1 / 9, next-page button, regenerate control, and order-hardcover link are present, with some controls below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: The book is there, but the typo in “Adventrue” makes it look unfinished. I also notice that the stated Pop-art comic style does not match the soft watercolour style I selected.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try to read through the book because that is the main purpose of this page.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the “›” next-page button and the 1 / 9 page indicator, although the order-hardcover link is below the fold.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. “›” indicates that I can continue reading, but there is no clear “Read next page” wording and the book controls require some guessing.

issues.title: Typo in generated title
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the finished book look careless and undermines my confidence in the rest of the story.
issues.fix: Correct the title to “The Magical Adventure of Sam” and provide a way to edit the title before ordering.

issues.title: Selected illustration style appears not to have been applied
issues.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” although the story setup said “soft watercolour illustrations.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I chose the visual style specifically, so this looks like the website ignored an important choice.
issues.fix: Apply the selected soft watercolour style, and clearly show which style was used or offer a correction option.

issues.title: Cover illustration may not reflect the supplied character details
issues.evidence: The cover shows a generic child labelled “Sam,” with no visible brown hair or connection to Grandpa Joe or the beach memory.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I expected a personalised family memory book, so a cover that does not visibly use the supplied details is disappointing.
issues.fix: Use the entered character details and memory in the generated cover, or clearly explain what personalisation is included and let me regenerate or edit it.

issues.title: Ordering control is below the fold
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can see that ordering exists, but I cannot immediately tell whether it is available without scrolling through the preview.
issues.fix: Keep a visible “Order hardcover” button near the book controls, or make the available actions clear at the top.

positives: The book title and page count are clearly displayed.
The page indicator “1 / 9” tells me how long the preview is.
The next-page button is visible and easy to find.
The preview is clearly separated as a generated result rather than another setup form.

output.output_reaction: I am disappointed that the generated book has the typo “Adventrue,” says “Pop-art comic” instead of the soft watercolour style I chose, and has a very generic cover that does not show the beach, yellow bucket, Grandpa Joe, or brown-haired Sam. I will still read all nine pages because I need to see whether the rest of the story uses the memory properly.
output.memory_note: The generated preview is 9 pages. It is titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam” and is labelled “Pop-art comic,” despite the selected soft watercolour style.
output.plan: Use the next-page arrow to read all nine generated pages carefully, checking whether Sam, Grandpa Joe, the beach, sandcastles, and the yellow bucket appear and whether the story is suitable for a five-year-old.

page_review.purpose: Review the hardcover order price, delivery and payment requirements before purchasing.
page_review.what_is_happening: The selected hardcover is shown with itemised pricing. A premium gift-wrap add-on is checked by default, increasing the total, and empty delivery and payment fields are presented. The order is not yet submitted.
page_review.first_impression: The main price is visible, but £45.97 feels high and the pre-ticked £7.99 gift wrap immediately looks like a sneaky add-on.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: I would try to inspect and remove the gift wrap, but I would not proceed with payment.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the checked “Premium gift wrap” checkbox, but it was easy to overlook because it appears as a compact row in the price breakdown.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The labels identify the hardcover, gift wrap, shipping and total clearly, but “Premium gift wrap” does not make clear that it is an optional extra I had not requested.

issues.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected without being requested
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the real cost higher without my consent and makes me distrust the checkout.
issues.fix: Default the optional gift-wrap checkbox to unchecked and show exactly what it adds to the total when selected.

issues.title: The final cost may be difficult to understand at a glance
issues.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99”, “Premium gift wrap £7.99”, “Shipping & handling £12.99”, and “Total £45.97”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can see the arithmetic, but £12.99 shipping is expensive and the page does not explain what delivery level or timeframe it provides.
issues.fix: Show a clear delivery estimate and explain whether shipping varies, while keeping every required and optional charge visibly itemised.

issues.title: The generated title contains a spelling error
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I would be embarrassed to receive a personalised book with such an obvious mistake in the title.
issues.fix: Correct the title to “Adventure” and allow the customer to edit or confirm the title before checkout.

positives: The hardcover price, shipping, add-on and total are shown as separate lines.
The delivery and payment sections are clearly labelled.
No payment has been submitted yet.

output.output_reaction: The checkout confirms that the generated book is the misspelled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”, but the cost is not reassuring: £45.97 with gift wrap, or £37.98 without it, plus an unexplained £12.99 shipping charge.
output.memory_note: Hardcover is £24.99; shipping and handling is £12.99. Premium gift wrap is pre-selected at £7.99, making the displayed total £45.97; without it, the arithmetic total is £37.98.
output.plan: Uncheck the optional premium gift wrap, then scroll through the remaining checkout content so I can see the final controls and any additional terms or charges. I will not fill in payment details or press “Pay now”.
